title: Generate Footprint Points
tagline: Export the sidecut as tip, RSL and tail point tables at equal arc-length spacing, each relative to its own origin -- for CNC, specs and spreadsheets.

slides.title: What it does
slides.problem: Shops and spec sheets want numbers, not curves. Generate Footprint Points splits the +Y outline at the contacts and samples each region evenly, in a table you can copy out.
useWhen: Send a sidecut to CNC or a supplier
slides.caption: GP1: 23 tip, 80 RSL and 23 tail points on S14.

slides.title: The dialog
params: FACE (the footprint face) / EDGES (edges or wires).
Off: the tip is the lower-X end; on: the higher-X end.
Units, decimal places ('sig figs'), units in cells, point counts 23 / 80 / 23, flips.
Keep the region curves / FCP-ACP planes; make sketches of the points.

slides.title: Example: GP1
slides.head: S14, RSL -750 ... 750
slides.body: Tip: 23 points x -924.567 ... -750 relative to the FCP; RSL: 80 points relative to the MRS; tail: 23 points relative to the ACP. All on the curve, spacing equal to 0.2 %.

keys: The region curves (empty unless Retain curves is on).
Reads tipEdgePoints / rslEdgePoints / tailEdgePoints / tableFormat stored on the origin (keep these stable).

items.head: Tip at +X
items.body: Turn on Tip toward +X; tip and tail swap with their origins (GP2).

items.head: Last one wins
items.body: The stored point lists are shared: the last Generate Footprint Points in the tree feeds the table.
